candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Numbers
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Numbers, on 9:1-14. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13. PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Numbers (c. 365 AD)

On the command to keep the Passover at its appointed season in the second year (Num 9:2), Ephrem reads the verse as establishing the canonical annual rhythm of Pascha: Passover is not a one-time deliverance but a perpetual yearly observance constitutive of covenant identity. The wilderness Passover anticipates every later celebration: in the desert, in the land, in exile, and finally in the eucharistic Pascha of the Church. Tewahedo Fasika observance cites Num 9:2 alongside Exo 12 as the canonical doubled-anchor for the non-negotiable yearly celebration; to skip Pascha is to step outside the covenant rhythm.

candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Numbers
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Numbers, on 9:15-23. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13. PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Numbers (c. 365 AD)

On the cloud covering the tabernacle by day and the appearance-of-fire by night (Num 9:15), Ephrem reads the doubled pillar — cloud and fire — as the canonical visible-sign of continuous divine indwelling: the Lord neither withdraws by day nor leaves the camp dark by night. The same cloud that veiled Sinai's fire now veils and reveals the tabernacle's glory. Tewahedo eucharistic theology cites Num 9:15 as the canonical anchor of the perpetual veil-and-glory pattern preserved in the curtained sanctuary: the tabot is veiled in cloud, illumined by lampstand fire, both signs of the abiding Lord.
